name: application-media
title: Media
description: Avatar-and-text layout patterns combining a thumbnail image with adjacent text content in various alignment configurations.
useWhen: Displaying a user avatar alongside a name, bio, or supporting text in a compact layout.
Building comment threads, activity feeds, or notification lists where each item has an avatar.
Combining a small thumbnail image with text metadata in a list or card component.
avoidWhen: The image is the primary content rather than a supporting thumbnail — use a dedicated image or gallery component.
Multiple images need to appear in a grid — use a grid or gallery layout instead.
The text content is long-form — a media object is designed for short metadata, not paragraphs.
responsiveBehavior: Media layouts stack the image above the text on very narrow viewports and return to the side-by-side arrangement on small screens and above.
accessibility: Avatar images must have meaningful alt text when they identify a person, or alt="" when decorative.
Do not use image position (left/right alignment) as the sole way to communicate meaning.
Ensure text beside the avatar has sufficient contrast and is not clipped at any zoom level.

variants.title: Left align top
variants.description: Image on the left, text top-aligned beside it — the classic media object for list rows and activity feeds.
accessibility: Avatar alt text should identify the person unless the name is already visible in the adjacent text.

variants.title: Left align center
variants.description: Image on the left, text vertically centered beside it — use when the image and text block are similar heights.
accessibility: Vertical alignment is decorative and carries no semantic meaning.

variants.title: Left align bottom
variants.description: Image on the left, text bottom-aligned — suitable when the text block is shorter than the image.
accessibility: Bottom alignment is decorative; ensure source reading order still makes logical sense.

variants.title: Left align stretch
variants.description: Image on the left, text area stretched to match the image height — creates a uniform block appearance.
accessibility: Stretch alignment is visual only; source order and semantic structure are unaffected.

variants.title: Right align top
variants.description: Image on the right, text top-aligned on the left — mirrors the standard media object for right-to-left emphasis.
accessibility: Ensure source order reflects the logical reading order regardless of visual alignment.

variants.title: Right align center
variants.description: Image on the right, text vertically centered on the left — for a balanced look when heights are similar.
accessibility: Vertical alignment is purely visual and does not affect screen reader reading order.

variants.title: Right align bottom
variants.description: Image on the right, text bottom-aligned on the left — use when the text block is shorter than the image.
accessibility: Bottom alignment is decorative; source reading order must still be logical.

variants.title: Right align stretch
variants.description: Image on the right, text area stretched to match the image height — mirrors the left stretch for right-image layouts.
accessibility: Stretch alignment is purely visual; semantic structure and reading order are unaffected.
